The members of the Cabinet (मंत्रिमंडल) Mission were Sir Pethick- Lawrence (Secretary for India), Stafford Cripps (Chairman- Board of Trade) and A.V . Alexander (Navy Minister). William Wood was not a member of the Cabinet Mission.

points.html: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 led to the formation of two independent and separate Dominions – India and Pakistan. The Princely States were provided three options – to join India, to join Pakistan or to remain Independent. *There were more than 560 princely States within the Indian territory, out of which most joined India, whereas three (Hyderabad, Junagadh and Kashmir) refused to join India. *Later on, Hyderabad through military Action, Junagadh through a referendum and Kashmir through the Instrument of Accession (a legal document) executed by Maharaja Hari Singh (ruler of the Jammu & Kashmir) were included in the Indian Union. The Indian Constitution that came into force in 1950 went a step further, recognising four different categories of States and territories in the first Schedule. Part A was comprised of former British India provinces, which had a governor and a Legislature. Part B was comprised of former Princely States governed by a 'raj pramukh' while Part C was a combination of Princely States and chief commissioner's provinces governed by a chief commissioner. Part D was comprised of the lone territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands administered by the President (राष्ट्रपति) through a Chief Commissioner/Other authority appointed by him. It was Part C states and part D territories that would go on to form the basis for the creation of Union Territories. *As per the Article 1(1) of the Constitution, “India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States” rather than the Federation of States. *Article 2 provides for the admission or establishment of New States. *Article 3 provides for the power of the Parliament in the formation of New States and alteration of areas, boundaries and names of existing States. *Parliament can form new States through a simple majority. *Amendments made under Articles 2 and 3 are out of the scope of Article 368. *Presently, India comprises 28 States and 8 Union Territories. S.K. Dhar Commission 1948 recommended the reorganization of States on the basis of administrative convenience instead of a linguistic basis. *In December 1948, the JVP committee was constituted by the Congress to scrutinize the recommendations of the S.K. Dhar Commission. *This committee included Jawahar Lal Nehru, Vallabh Bhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramaiya. *The committee, in its report presented in April 1949, officially rejected the demand for the reorganization of the States on linguistic basis.

India, like Britain, adopted the system of single citizenship (नागरिकता).

The Indian Citizenship Act was passed by Parliament (संसद) in 1955.
It prescribes five ways of acquiring citizenship (नागरिकता) – (1) By Birth, (2) By Descent, (3) By Registration, (4) By Naturalisation and (5) By incorporation of territory.

The Indian Citizenship (नागरिकता) Act 1955, prescribes three ways of losing citizenship, whether acquired under the Act or prior to it under the Constitution – (1) By Renunciation, (2) By Termination and (3) By Deprivation.

(2) Mandamus (We command) – It is a command issued by the court against a public official, any public body, a corporation, an inferior court, a tribunal or a government, asking them to perform official duties that one has failed or refused to perform. (4) Certiorari (to be certified) – It is issued on the grounds of excess of jurisdiction or lack of jurisdiction or error of law. It is issued by a higher court to a lower court to transfer a case pending with the latter to itself or to quash the order of the latter in a case. points.html: The President (राष्ट्रपति) of India is the head of the Indian State, the first citizen, and acts as the symbol of unity, integrity and solidarity of the nation. *According to Article 52, ‘There shall be a President of India’. *According to Article 53, the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President and shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with this Constitution. *According to Article 54, the President shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the Legislative Assembly of the States. *70th Amendment Act, 1992 (effective from 01- 06-1995) provided for the inclusion of the elected members D–156 General Studies Indian Polity and Governance of legislative assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union territory of Puducherry in the electoral college for the election of the President. *Nominated members and members of Legislative Councils do not participate in the election of the President. *According to Article 55(3), the election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and the voting is done by secret ballot. *All doubts and disputes in connection with the election of the President are enquired into and decided by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final. *The Election of the President cannot be challenged on the grounds that the electoral college was incomplete. (due to any vacancy of members) *Article 58 describes the eligibility criteria (a citizen of India, has completed the age of 35 years and is qualified for election as a member of the House of the People, and is not ineligible due to holding any office of profit under Article 58(2)) for election as President.

points.html: The Maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250. According to Article 80, the Rajya Sabha consists of not more than 238 members from the States and Union Territories (elected indirectly) and 12 other members are nominated by the President (राष्ट्रपति) from amongst the persons having special knowledge or practical experience in the field of literature, science, art and social service (Present Strength is 245, out of which 12 are nominated members). *Representatives of each state shall be elected by the elected members of the legislative assembly of the state in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. *Only 3 Union territories (Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir) out of 8 have representatives in Rajya Sabha. *Rajya Sabha is a Permanent house. Hence it is not subject to dissolution. *As nearly as possible 1/3rd members of the Rajya Sabha retire at the end of every second year. *The term of its members is 6 years. *A Person to be elected as a member of Rajya Sabha must fulfil two criteria- (1) he must be a citizen of India and (2) he must not be less than 30 years of age. In addition to the prior two conditions, he must be an elector for a parliamentary constituency in India. *The Vice-President of India is the ex- officio chairman of the Council of States/Upper House of Parliament. *When the Vice-President acts as the President he shall not be entitled to get the salary and allowances of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha. For this period, he receives salary and allowances of the President. *Rajya Sabha elects a deputy chairman from amongst its members. *The Deputy Chairman gives his resignation in writing to the Chairman. *Rajya Sabha has the power to remove the Deputy Chairman from his post, by a resolution passed by the absolute majority of the total members of Rajya Sabha. Such resolution can be moved only after giving at least 14 days' notice. *When the post of Chairman is vacant, the deputy chairman will perform the duties of the chairman. *While presiding over the Rajya Sabha, the Deputy Chairman can't vote in general, he can only exercise a casting vote in case of a tie. *When a resolution to remove the Vice- President from his office is under consideration, he will not be presiding as the Chairman and when a resolution of removal of the Deputy Chairman is under consideration, he will not be presiding as the Deputy Chairman. *The representation of states in Rajya Sabha is given in proportion to their population. *For a quorum, there must be the presence of one-tenth of the total number of members in the Rajya Sabha. *The Representation of People Act 1951 (through an amendment in 2003) made a provision that any person can contest from anywhere for Rajya Sabha even if he is a resident of any other state. Now for contesting Rajya Sabha elections, a person must be an elector in a parliamentary constituency anywhere in India. *The 4th Schedule of the Indian Constitution enumerates the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats for states and union territories. *Article 249 states that if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with a 2/3 majority of its members present and voting, the Parliament can make laws in the national interest regarding the subjects of the state list, which are specified in the resolution. *It is valid for a period of 1 year, but it can be extended by passing a resolution.

points.html: The President (राष्ट्रपति) Rule under Article 356 is imposed in case of failure of the Constitutional machinery in the State. *Notably in the case of the President’s Rule the President can act either on a report of the Governor or otherwise too (i.e even without the Governor's report). *Under this arrangement the President may acquire all or any of the powers of the state government concerned. *The President (actually on behalf of him, the Governor)dismisses the state council of ministers headed by the Chief Minister. *During this time the Parliament passes the state legislative bills and the state budget. *A Proclamation imposing Presidential Rule must be approved by both the Houses of the Parliament within two months from the date of its issue. *If approved by both the Houses of the Parliament the President's rule continues for 6 months. *It can be extended for a maximum period of 3 years with the approval of the Parliament, every six months. *Every resolution approving the proclamation of President’s Rule or its continuance can be passed by either house of the Parliament only by a simple majority.
